# windows_partition (Resource)

Manages one partition on a data disk on a remote Windows host via SSH and PowerShell (`New-Partition` / `Get-Partition` / `Resize-Partition` / `Set-Partition` / `Remove-Partition`), including its drive letter.

Identity is `<disk_unique_id>|<guid>` on GPT disks and `<disk_unique_id>|<offset>` on MBR disks (partitions have no GUID there): the scan-time partition number is informational only and never used to find the partition.

Deleting the resource **destroys the partition and its data** (`Remove-Partition`): consider `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }` for partitions holding data. Protected partitions (boot, system, EFI, MSR, recovery, or holding the active pagefile — or whose placement cannot be determined, fail closed) are refused with `protected_storage`.

Typical layering is `windows_disk` → `windows_partition` → `windows_volume` (#292): adopt and initialize the disk, carve the partition, then format it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    windows = {
      source  = "kfrlabs/windows"
      version = "~> 0.1"
    }
  }
}

provider "windows" {
  host     = var.windows_host
  username = var.windows_username
  password = var.windows_password
}

# Minimal example: carve a data partition from the largest free extent of an
# adopted disk and give it a drive letter. The partition is always created
# with -AssignDriveLetter:$false first, then the configured letter is assigned
# explicitly (no random letters, no Explorer "format disk" race).
resource "windows_partition" "data" {
  disk_unique_id   = windows_disk.data.id
  use_maximum_size = true
  drive_letter     = "E"
  gpt_type         = "basic_data"
}

# Advanced example: carve an explicitly sized partition at the first fitting
# extent, without a drive letter. Growing later is in-place (set a larger
# size_bytes); shrinking is refused with shrink_not_supported in v1.
# Deleting the resource destroys the partition and its data: consider
# `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }` for partitions holding data.
resource "windows_partition" "sized" {
  disk_unique_id = windows_disk.data.id
  size_bytes     = 10737418240 # 10 GiB

  lifecycle {
    prevent_destroy = true
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `disk_unique_id` (String) Stable Get-Disk UniqueId of the hosting disk (e.g. the `id` of a `windows_disk` resource). ForceNew: a different disk is a different partition.

### Optional

- `drive_letter` (String) Single drive letter D-Z (upper-cased), assigned explicitly after creation (`Set-Partition -NewDriveLetter`; removal via `Remove-PartitionAccessPath`). Null removes the letter. A, B and C are rejected (floppy- and system-reserved). A letter already in use is a `drive_letter_in_use` error.
- `gpt_type` (String) GPT partition type: alias `basic_data` (default, `{ebd0a0a2-b9e5-4433-87c0-68b6b72699c7}`), `msr`, `recovery`, or a literal GUID. GPT disks only (validated against the disk style at apply). ForceNew. Conflicts with `mbr_type`. Aliases are stored and planned in canonical GUID form.
- `is_active` (Boolean) Whether the partition is active (`Set-Partition -IsActive`). MBR only. Null (unset) leaves the observed state unmanaged.
- `is_hidden` (Boolean) Whether the partition is hidden (`Set-Partition -IsHidden`). Null (unset) leaves the observed state unmanaged.
- `mbr_type` (String) MBR partition type byte: alias `IFS` (default, `0x07`), `FAT32`, `FAT32_LBA`, `EXTENDED`, `NTFS`, a hex byte (`0x00`-`0xFF`) or a decimal byte (`0`-`255`). MBR disks only (validated against the disk style at apply). ForceNew. Conflicts with `gpt_type`. Aliases and decimal bytes are stored and planned in canonical `0x..` form.
- `offset_bytes` (Number) Explicit partition offset in bytes (`New-Partition -Offset`). Null (default) places the partition at the first fitting extent. ForceNew.
- `size_bytes` (Number) Desired partition size in bytes. Grows in place (`Resize-Partition`, which extends the file system with it for NTFS/ReFS); shrinking is refused with `shrink_not_supported` in v1. Conflicts with `use_maximum_size`.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))
- `use_maximum_size` (Boolean) Create the partition from the largest free extent (`-UseMaximumSize`) instead of an explicit `size_bytes`. Create-only (ForceNew): later growth is not automatic (set `size_bytes` to grow).

### Read-Only

- `access_paths` (List of String) Get-Partition AccessPaths, as observed on the host.
- `guid` (String) Get-Partition Guid, as observed on the host. The stable identity on GPT disks; empty on MBR disks (whose identity is the offset).
- `id` (String) Resource identifier: `<disk_unique_id>|<guid>` on GPT, `<disk_unique_id>|<offset>` on MBR.
- `is_boot` (Boolean) Whether the partition is the boot partition, as observed on the host. Boot partitions are refused with protected_storage.
- `is_system` (Boolean) Whether the partition is the system partition, as observed on the host. System partitions are refused with protected_storage.
- `operational_status` (String) Get-Partition OperationalStatus (e.g. Online), as observed on the host.
- `partition_number` (Number) Get-Partition PartitionNumber, as observed on the host. Scan-time assignment, informational only: identity never relies on it.

### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import an existing partition by its "<disk_unique_id>|<guid_or_offset>" ID
# (the GUID on GPT disks, the byte offset on MBR disks).
terraform import windows_partition.data 'SCSI\DISK&VEN_MSFT&PROD_VIRTUAL_DISK&REV_1.0|EBD0A0A2-B9E5-4433-87C0-68B6B72699C7'
```
